```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 12
    n_vehicles = 4
    Q = 77  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[72, 64], [59, 41], [42, 89], [86, 14], [36, 65], [69, 53], [64, 7], [86, 64], [5, 74], [8, 49], [56, 38], [12, 77]]
    demands = [19, 22, 20, 10, 14, 19, 15, 20, 11, 15, 25, 16]
    time_windows = [[0, 323], [25, 76], [7, 68], [60, 146], [48, 136], [37, 94], [21, 77], [57, 157], [52, 112], [76, 152], [59, 130], [22, 116], [46, 101]]
    service_times = [8, 10, 7, 15, 9, 9, 6, 9, 15, 14, 14, 5]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Distribution Planning and Field Operations
From: Logistics Operations Manager
Subject: Routing and scheduling plan with time windows and capacity constraints

Overview
We will dispatch a small fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a central depot to serve a defined set of customers. All vehicles will depart the depot at time 0 and each will run a single trip: leave the depot, visit an assigned sequence of customers, and return to the depot before the facility’s latest allowable return time. Travel time between any two locations will be treated as the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with an implicit speed of 1, so one unit of distance equals one unit of time.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
- Every customer must be visited exactly once by exactly one vehicle.
- Each customer has an acceptable delivery time window. The start of unloading must occur within that window.
- If a vehicle arrives before a customer’s window opens, the driver must wait on site until the window opens before beginning service.
- Each stop requires a defined unloading/service time. After serving a customer, the vehicle departs at the time service completes. If the vehicle waited for a window to open, service begins at window open and the departure is at window open plus service time.
- All vehicles must finish their routes and return to the depot before the depot’s closing time for the planning horizon.

Capacity and Operating Constraints
- Vehicles are identical and have the same carrying capacity. The total customer demand assigned to any one route must not exceed the vehicle’s capacity.
- No vehicle performs multiple trips; there are no mid-route replenishments or customer split deliveries.
- The feasible sequence of visits for each route is constrained by the need to meet both capacity limits and customer time windows, including any required waiting times.

Cost Structure
- Each vehicle used incurs a fixed deployment cost, in addition to travel distance costs accrued along its route.
- The routing plan must balance the trade-off between using more vehicles (to better align with tight time windows and reduce distance) and minimizing travel distance and fixed deployment costs.

Goal
Develop a set of vehicle routes and schedules that:
- Serve every customer exactly once,
- Respect all time windows and service times,
- Keep the total demand on each route within vehicle capacity,
- Start all vehicles at time 0 and return them to the depot before it closes,
- Minimize the combined total of travel distance and vehicle deployment costs.

Assumptions and Notes
- Vehicles are interchangeable (same capacity and performance).
- Distances and times are based on straight-line movement between coordinate points with no additional congestion or speed variations.
- Waiting at customers is allowed only to satisfy the earliest start of the time window; late arrivals are not permitted.

Next Steps
- Confirm the operations data in the annex.
- Generate a feasible routing plan that satisfies the constraints above.
- Review the trade-offs between distance and number of vehicles deployed to ensure cost-effective, on-time performance.
